thread.title: Reduce escalation time without unauthorized credits

arrival.reason: A Canadian policy-freshness incident exposed a gap between the service's intended authority and its implemented behavior.
arrival.consequence: Canadian cases remain recommendation-only until the policy boundary and evidence obligations are explicit.

moments.title: You are here because service intent and live behavior diverged.
moments.message: I can use the incident as evidence for a new service definition, or we can begin from a clean business intent. I will preserve the source either way.
moments.question: What should anchor this work thread?

options.label: Use the observed incident
options.description: Start with verified production evidence and reconstruct intended behavior.

options.label: Start from business intent
options.description: Frame the outcome first and use the incident later as supporting evidence.

moments.consequence: This choice establishes provenance; it does not determine the solution.

moments.title: Define success before defining an agent.
moments.message: The live evidence suggests the desired outcome is faster, policy-correct escalation resolution—while preserving accountable financial approval.
moments.question: Which completion boundary represents the business outcome?

options.label: Resolved or safely transferred
options.description: Complete only when the customer receives an approved resolution or an accountable specialist owns the transfer.

options.label: Recommendation produced
options.description: End the service when a recommendation is generated, leaving completion outside the service contract.

moments.consequence: The boundary determines ownership, outcome measurement, and which failures remain inside the service.

moments.title: The work is becoming an inspectable service contract.
moments.message: The service now spans evidence assembly, policy determination, recommendation, human approval, controlled execution, customer communication, and outcome observation.
moments.question: Should policy ambiguity remain inside the service or transfer immediately?

options.label: Transfer with evidence
options.description: Route ambiguity to the policy owner with the conflicting sources and case context attached.

options.label: Let the model rank policies
options.description: Allow the service to select the highest-ranked policy even when authoritative sources conflict.

moments.consequence: This choice changes the service sketch, ownership boundary, failure modes, and test obligations.

moments.title: A policy rule cannot remain a hidden inference.
moments.message: Observed behavior shows a global policy can outrank a newer Canadian policy. I propose: jurisdiction and effective date take precedence; unresolved conflicts transfer to the policy owner before recommendation.
moments.question: How should this proposition enter the draft?

options.label: Accept as draft
options.description: Record the rule as an explicit draft decision and require domain confirmation.

options.label: Contest the proposition
options.description: Keep the clause unresolved and document the competing interpretation.

moments.consequence: Accepting a draft is not approval; it creates accountable verification work.

moments.eyebrow: Bring expertise to the exact decision
moments.title: Priya does not need the whole portal—only the policy decision.
moments.message: I prepared a focused request with the proposed clause, conflicting evidence, affected Canadian cohort, and the consequence of accepting or rejecting it.
moments.question: Send the contribution request and incorporate the domain response?

options.label: Ask Priya in context
options.description: Capture her confirmation, source citation, and one required exception without losing the thread.

options.label: Defer and assign
options.description: Keep the gap visible and continue only under a constrained draft state.

moments.consequence: The contribution becomes part of the decision ledger, not a detached comment.

moments.title: Technical capability is not permission to act.
moments.message: The imported implementation can call the credit and case APIs. The proposed service authority must be narrower than that capability.
moments.question: Which authority envelope should the Trusted Draft carry?

options.label: Recommend; human approves credit
options.description: The service may update case notes, but every financial action requires a current human approval.

options.label: Auto-issue credits under $50
options.description: Delegate low-value financial execution within policy and confidence thresholds.

moments.consequence: This decision binds actions, execution identity, approvals, audit receipts, and negative test obligations.

moments.title: The service is coherent enough to compose—not yet safe to release.
moments.message: Outcome, boundary, evidence, authority, responsibilities, and rehearsal obligations now form one versioned working agreement. One domain exception remains visible and assigned.
moments.question: Commit this version as the Trusted Draft?

options.label: Commit Trusted Draft
options.description: Freeze the shared agreement and continue into service composition with causal lineage preserved.

options.label: Review material decisions
options.description: Return to the decision ledger before composition begins.

moments.consequence: Commitment authorizes composition work only. Release authority remains blocked until evidence obligations pass.

clauses.statement: Reduce eligible escalation cycle time while improving policy-correct resolution.
Complete when the customer receives an approved resolution or an accountable specialist owns the transfer.
Use case, account, jurisdiction, transaction date, and the authoritative effective policy.
Transfer unresolved policy conflicts to the policy owner with evidence attached.
Jurisdiction and effective date take precedence over global retrieval rank.
The service recommends a remedy; a human approves every financial action.
Pass Canadian effective-date, policy-conflict, missing-policy, permission-isolation, and approval-linkage scenarios.

gaps.title: Confirm Canadian precedence and exception rule
